readerTitle: Your bakery on someone else's app: four calls in a row
caseNote: 가상 시뮬레이션 (지역 베이커리 체인 본사 안의 성장팀이 배달 앱 플랫폼에 입점하는 이야기) · 모든 수치와 회사는 설명용
insight: 남의 플랫폼에 올라타는 것은 한 번의 결정이 아니라 계속 이어지는 협상이다. 매 단계에서 플랫폼에 기대는 정도와 빠져나올 길을 함께 관리해야 한다.
misconception: 큰 플랫폼에 들어가면 고객이 생기니 무조건 이득이다. 반대로, 플랫폼이 조건을 바꾸면 바로 빠져나오는 것이 답이다.

sources.text: 플랫폼 리스크, 게이트키퍼, 보완재 상품화(commoditize your complement) 등 사업모델 분야의 표준 개념
모든 회사, 수치, 수수료율은 설명용 가상 예시

factChecks.note: 모든 수치는 가상입니다. 계산 확인: $20 주문 기준 수수료 25% = $5, 30% = $6. 실제 배달 앱의 수수료율을 암시하지 않도록 카드에 '가상' 라벨을 유지하세요.
영수증·포장에 자체 주문 안내를 넣는 행위는 플랫폼 약관에 따라 금지될 수 있습니다. 카드에 'where the app's terms allow'로 조건을 달았습니다. 특정 국가의 법률 조언으로 읽히지 않는지 검토하세요.
배달 앱이 자체 브랜드(가상 주방 등)를 운영하는 것은 업계에서 관찰되는 일반적 패턴으로만 서술했습니다. 특정 기업 사례로 바꾸려면 1차 출처가 필요합니다.

cards.title: Your bakery on someone else's app: four calls in a row
body: Mara runs a three-person growth team at a regional bakery-café chain with 40 stores. Head office has one question for her: should we sell through the big delivery app everyone uses?
The app has millions of hungry customers. It also writes the rules. You'll make Mara's next four decisions.

image.label: A bakery storefront inside a giant phone screen
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 거대한 스마트폰 화면 안에 작은 베이커리 가게가 들어가 있고, 화면 밖에서 큰 손이 앱 화면의 순서를 손가락으로 옮기는 장면. 실제 배달 앱 로고나 색상은 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: Join the app?
body: The app takes 25% of each order. Your own ordering site works, but few people find it. What does Mara recommend?

options.text: List all 40 stores and move the marketing budget into in-app promotions
options.feedback: You get reach fast, but you also hand the app most of your growth before you know whether app orders even make money.

options.text: List 8 stores for three months, track what each order leaves after the cut, and keep the own site running
options.feedback: You learn the real economics cheaply and keep a second door open. The cost is slower growth while you test.

options.text: Stay off and build a full delivery app of your own
options.feedback: You keep full control, but you pay to build something customers may never download. Control without reach is expensive.

cards.title: The app changes the deal.
body: Say you chose the test. It works, and a year later app orders are a big share of delivery sales.
Then the app announces a new rate: 30% for partners who don't buy ads. On a $20 order, its cut rises from $5 to $6.

options.text: Buy the ads to keep your ranking and the old rate
options.feedback: Sales stay steady, but you now pay twice for the same customers, and the next change will find you even more dependent.

options.text: Raise in-app prices a little, and invite repeat customers to order direct where the app's terms allow
options.feedback: You protect the margin and slowly move loyal customers to a channel you own. You may lose some price-sensitive app orders.
It feels like taking back control, but you drop a large share of sales overnight with no channel ready to replace them.

cards.title: The platform owns the door, so it sets the price of walking through.
body: When you build on a platform you don't control, you gain its customers but accept **platform risk**: the owner can change fees, rankings or rules, and you have to adapt.

Your exposure grows with one number: the share of your sales that only reaches you through that door. Mara's real job isn't to avoid the app. It's to keep that share at a level the bakery can survive losing.

image.label: A dial showing share of sales through the app
image.brief: 계기판 형태의 다이얼 인포그래픽. 바늘이 "Sales through the app" 비율을 가리키고, 낮은 구간은 초록 "Useful channel", 높은 구간은 빨강 "They set your terms". 실제 수치는 넣지 않음.

cards.softwareNote: The same thing happens to software built on an app store, a marketplace or another company's API. A fee change or a new review rule can reshape your margins overnight, so track how much revenue depends on each one.

cards.title: An offer that sounds generous.
body: Say you chose to adjust prices and build the direct channel. Now the app makes an offer: drop the rate to 22% if your stores list on no other delivery app.

options.text: Accept. It's the cheapest rate on the table
options.feedback: You save now, but the app becomes your only gate to delivery customers. When the contract ends, it can name any price.

options.text: Decline and stay on several apps plus your own site
options.feedback: You pay a higher rate, but no single gatekeeper can squeeze you, because customers can still reach you other ways.

options.text: Accept for 10 stores only, for one year, with a clear exit clause
options.feedback: A limited bet that tests the savings. Just make sure the exit clause is real and that you could actually leave in time.

cards.title: The app starts selling croissants.
body: Say you declined. Months later, the app launches its own bakery brand, made in shared kitchens, priced below yours and shown above you in search.
The app gains when bakeries look interchangeable. Then customers shop by price and convenience, which it controls.

options.text: Match its prices to win back the top spot
options.feedback: You play the one game the app always wins. Your margins shrink, and you look even more like everyone else.

options.text: Lean into what it can't copy: signature items, the café visit, and office catering booked direct
options.feedback: You give up some app orders, but your brand becomes a reason to seek you out, which moves you off the price list.

options.text: Quit the app and put everything into your own site
options.feedback: This makes sense if direct orders are already strong. If not, you trade one risk for a sudden drop in sales.

cards.title: Hedging has a price too.
body: Running your own site, several apps and a loyalty scheme costs money and attention. For a small business, one good platform may simply be the best deal available.
The goal isn't zero dependence. It's knowing what each order leaves you, having a plan if the rules change, and not making your own brand harder to find.
And the app isn't a villain. Its interests overlap with yours, until they don't.

cards.title: Use the platform's reach, but keep a door it doesn't own.
body: Each of Mara's calls maps to an idea from this unit.
list: **Join with a test:** you're a complement to the platform, and you can choose how much to rely on it
**Fee change:** platform risk grows with the share of sales it controls
**Exclusive deal:** don't make one gatekeeper your only way in
**Its own bakery brand:** platforms gain by making you interchangeable, so make yourself hard to swap
cards.callout: **Try it today:** write down what share of your sales arrives through a channel you don't own, and what you'd do if its fee rose by a fifth.
